This is supported by two distinct pathways, both of which involve the lowest common ancestor 3-Oxo-Delta(4) Steroid. Both pathways converge on the same receptor, indicating a shared mechanism of action involving steroid hormone binding. The evidence suggests that Medroxyprogesterone Acetate may influence Nr3c1 through its role as a steroid hormone, potentially affecting receptor activity and downstream biological processes. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as both paths have relatively low scores, but they collectively highlight a consistent link between Medroxyprogesterone Acetate and Nr3c1 through the binding of steroid hormones. The mechanisms involve the interaction of steroid hormones with Nr3c1, which is a key component in the regulation of gene expression and cellular function.
